name: dispatch_resource_or_fallback
description: Looks up a resource by a fixed numeric identifier through a library jump table. If a handle comes back it is passed with two parameters to a second library entry point and then released, otherwise a no-argument fallback entry point is called.

name: call_entry_without_args
description: Makes one call through the library jump table to an entry point that takes no arguments, then returns. Its only behaviour is that forwarding call.

name: dispatch_resource_second_entry
description: Performs the same resource lookup as its neighbouring routine, but passes the found handle with two parameters to a different library entry point before releasing it. The no-argument fallback is used when the lookup fails.

name: call_entry_no_arguments
description: Makes a single no-argument call through the library jump table and returns. The routine has no other effect and is entered from a data pointer.

name: lookup_resource_with_secondary_id
description: Looks up a resource by a fixed identifier and, if it is absent, looks up a second fixed identifier instead. The handle found is passed with two parameters to a library entry point and then released; a found first handle is handled the same way through a different entry point.

name: dispatch_record_resource_handle
description: Looks up a resource using an identifier paired with a field read from a caller-supplied record, and stores the handle back into that record. It passes the handle and two other record fields to a library entry point and then releases the handle.

name: plot_symmetric_offset_pairs
description: Makes one no-argument library call, then steps a counter and, for each step, calls two alternating library entry points twice each with a symmetric pair of offsets around a centre value. The unnamed call targets and the mirrored offsets are the only evidence of its behaviour.

name: plot_symmetric_pairs_stepped
description: Advances an accumulator by a stepped count held in a record and, for each step, calls two library entry points with mirrored offsets around a centre value. The loop ends when its counter reaches zero.

name: plot_symmetric_pairs_until_negative
description: Performs the same mirrored-offset calls as its sibling routine but with the exit test placed at the end of the loop, so the loop stops once its counter goes negative. It updates the stored step values after each set of calls.

name: blit_masked_plane_rows
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then for each of four bitplanes writes a fill word of all ones or all zeros chosen from a bit mask, together with source, modulo and size registers. The DMA control register is written with the blitter-enable bit set, and the DMA status register is polled for blitter-busy.

name: blit_plane_rows_with_mask
description: Writes custom-chip blitter registers for each bitplane in turn, selecting an all-ones or all-zeros fill word from a bit mask and waiting on blitter-busy between planes. The loop advances the destination pointer by a plane size on each pass.

name: blit_plane_rows_early_exit
description: Performs the same per-plane blitter register writes as its sibling routine but leaves the loop as soon as the mask shifts to zero, rather than after a fixed number of planes. It waits on blitter-busy before each write.

name: advance_seeded_counter_value
description: On first use it initialises a stored 32-bit value from a 16-bit data slot, then adds the result of a no-argument library call plus one to that value. It returns the upper 24 bits of the stored value.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Does nothing except call one other routine and return. The routine adds no logic of its own.

name: write_dma_control_register
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so this description rests only on the listed facts: the routine touches the DMA control register, and writes to it enable DMA channels when bit 15 is set. Its exact effect depends on the value written, which is not visible here.

name: wait_until_flag_cleared
description: Spins in a loop reading a 16-bit flag from the base-relative data area and returns once the flag reads zero. It has no other side effects.

name: set_flag_after_optional_calls
description: Calls one library entry point when a first status word is nonzero, calls it again when a second status word is nonzero, then sets the 16-bit flag at the same offset that the wait routine polls to all ones.

name: call_routine_twice
description: Calls one other routine twice in a row and returns. Only that repeated call sequence is visible.

name: blit_rectangle_across_five_planes
description: Computes a word width and a row height from two corner coordinate pairs, enables the blitter in the DMA control register, then loops five times, once per bitplane. Each pass offsets the source and destination pointers by one plane size and programs blitter control, size and modulo registers.

name: program_blitter_pointers_per_plane
description: Loops a counted number of times, waiting on blitter-busy before each pass. Each pass copies two pointer values into blitter pointer registers, sets a modulo register and advances the source pointers by one plane size.

name: program_blitter_pointers_then_wait
description: Copies two pointer values into blitter pointer registers, sets a modulo register and advances the source pointers by one plane size, then waits on blitter-busy before the next pass. The loop runs a counted number of times.

name: call_routine_fixed_block_rows
description: Passes a pointer offset from a base address, a stored value, zero and a fixed row count of 45 to a second routine. The routine is not reached by any caller in the facts.

name: call_routine_on_row_span
description: Computes a byte offset from a row index multiplied by a 40-byte row stride, adds it to a base pointer, and passes that pointer with a stored value, zero and the difference between two stored counts to a second routine.

name: call_routine_row_span_swapped
description: Makes the same row-offset calculation as its sibling routine but passes the stored value first and the computed pointer second. The final argument is the difference between two stored counts.

name: request_block_with_fallback
description: Requests a memory block from a library entry point using a fixed attribute word, and calls a no-argument fallback routine if the request returns nothing. The result of the request is returned to the caller.

name: return_stored_long_value
description: Returns a 32-bit value read from a fixed slot in the base-relative data area. It has no other effect.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it performs no work and is a stub.

name: forward_two_args_to_library
description: Passes its two parameters unchanged to one library entry point and returns.

name: set_interrupt_and_dma_controls
description: Calls two no-argument routines around the setup, writes control words that set bits in the interrupt-enable and DMA control registers, and then clears low DMA channel bits. In between it calls a library entry with a count and a record pointer.

name: store_result_of_library_call
description: Calls one library entry point with a fixed argument of two and stores the returned value in a base-relative data slot.

name: open_libraries_and_input_device
description: Opens two named system libraries and calls a no-argument fallback routine if either fails to open. It then reads a field from one library base, calls further library routines, and sets up an I/O request on the input device before writing an interrupt-related control word.

name: release_pointers_with_fixed_sizes
description: Walks a table of records and, for each non-null pointer, calls a library entry point with that pointer and a scaled value. It then calls the same entry point for a fixed list of pointers paired with constant sizes, skipping any null pointer.

name: close_pointers_after_routine
description: Calls one library entry with a stored pointer, calls another routine, then passes two further stored pointers to a second library entry point. The routine has no other logic.

name: copy_bytes_overlap_safe
description: Copies a counted block of bytes from source to destination. When the source lies below the destination it copies from the end so overlapping regions are preserved, otherwise it copies forward.

name: copy_bytes_forward_counted
description: Copies bytes one at a time from source to destination, decrementing a counter until it reaches minus one. A count of zero still copies one byte.

name: copy_words_overlap_safe
description: Copies a counted block of 16-bit words from source to destination. It copies from the end when the source lies below the destination so overlapping regions are preserved, otherwise it copies forward.

name: copy_words_forward_counted
description: Copies 16-bit words one at a time from source to destination, decrementing a counter until it reaches minus one. A count of zero still copies one word.

name: return_absolute_value
description: Returns the magnitude of a signed 16-bit value by negating it when it is negative and returning it unchanged otherwise.

name: return_absolute_long_value
description: Returns the magnitude of a signed 32-bit value by negating it when it is negative and returning it unchanged otherwise.

name: multiply_halves_then_divide
description: Multiplies the two 16-bit halves of its first argument, then divides that product by the low 16 bits of its second argument. The result packs the remainder into the upper 16 bits and the quotient into the lower 16 bits.

name: sum_squares_of_halves
description: Returns the sum of the squares of the two 16-bit halves of its argument.

name: multiply_argument_halves
description: Returns the product of the two 16-bit halves of its argument.

name: fetch_six_values_into_fields
description: Calls a routine in three pairs, each pair using a different stored input, and writes the six 16-bit results into consecutive slots of the base-relative data area.

name: shift_stored_word_pair
description: Makes three calls, then stores the value returned by a further call into one slot and the previously held slot value into a second slot, moving a pair of stored words along.

name: store_pair_after_three_calls
description: Makes three calls, two of them with a stored input, then writes the returned low word and the first argument into the two words of the caller's record.

name: stub_no_operation_return
description: Contains only a return, so it performs no work.

name: lookup_quadrant_table_value
description: Reduces its argument into a half-turn range of a 360-step cycle using quadrant reflection, looks up a 16-bit value in a table in the base-relative data area, and negates it when a mode flag is clear. The argument is first offset by 360 units.

name: lookup_quadrant_table_unshifted
description: Performs the same quadrant reflection and table lookup as its sibling routine, but uses the argument directly without the 360-unit offset.

name: project_four_coordinates_by_depth
description: Adds 600 to a depth value, then computes four quotients of coordinate differences and sums, each shifted left by nine bits before division by the depth. The results are stored in four base-relative slots.

name: project_pair_by_depth
description: Computes two quotients, each a shifted coordinate sum divided by a depth value offset by 600, and stores them in two base-relative slots.

name: add_packed_decimal_digits
description: Adds the bytes of a second value to the corresponding bytes of a four-byte packed-decimal buffer, applying decimal adjustment after each addition so the buffer stays in binary-coded decimal.

name: accumulate_packed_decimal_maximum
description: Stores its argument, adds four bytes of packed-decimal digits from one buffer into another with decimal adjustment, keeps the larger of the accumulated value and a running maximum, and then calls a second routine.

name: increment_packed_decimal_byte
description: Adds one to a packed-decimal byte in the base-relative data area with decimal adjustment, then calls another routine.

name: project_fixed_length_table
description: Projects each entry of a fixed-length table by shifting its coordinate left by nine bits and dividing by a depth value offset by 600. It adds a base offset to one coordinate and writes the results as interleaved pairs into an output buffer.

name: store_projected_pair_to_buffer
description: Makes one call and then writes two stored 16-bit values into the buffer that the caller points to.

name: apply_scaled_offsets_to_table
description: Adds scaled multiples of a stored scalar to three interleaved word fields of a table in three passes. It also sets three flag bytes according to whether a stored offset is above a fixed threshold of minus 500.

name: copy_offset_word_pairs
description: Makes calls to prepare three copy passes, each moving word pairs from one table to another while adding or subtracting a fixed offset of 30 and stepping through the destination. A routine result controls each loop's exit.

name: project_points_with_depth_guard
description: Sets point counts from stored values, adjusting them when a flag is set, and emits three words per row through a helper when a motion flag is clear. It then projects each point by shifting its coordinates by nine bits and dividing by a depth offset by 600, substituting one for a zero depth.

name: relay_single_routine_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code exists. The listed facts show one call to another routine and an entry through a handler pointer, and nothing more about its purpose can be stated.

name: transform_and_project_vertex_rows
description: Repeatedly combines coordinate triples with two scalar multipliers using sums and differences, then divides each resulting pair by a depth value offset by 600. The quotients are written to an output buffer, and the routine moves to the next row group when its counter reaches zero.

name: copy_table_with_derived_entries
description: Copies a table entry by entry into an output buffer, calling a helper routine for each value, then fills several derived entries by copying earlier values at fixed positions. When the argument is nonzero it also fills a run of entries with a value offset by 300.

name: store_argument_word
description: Stores the low 16-bit word of its argument in a base-relative data slot.

name: set_flag_dependent_slot_values
description: Sets four word slots to default values, then overrides each one when the matching flag bit of the argument is set, and copies the results into several further slots. Per-bit negated byte flags are also recorded.

name: store_doubled_bound_differences
description: Stores two input words, then computes a value from doubled differences between those inputs and four stored bounds and writes it to a slot.

name: store_bound_differences_only
description: Computes the same doubled bound differences as its sibling routine and writes the result to a slot, without storing the input words.

name: clip_line_edge_intersection
description: Selects rectangle edges using flag bits and computes where a line crosses each one by multiplying a stored difference and dividing by a slope value. It returns the first crossing that lies within the stored range.

name: find_line_edge_crossing
description: Computes where a line crosses an edge chosen by flag bits, using the same multiply-then-divide approach as its sibling routine. It returns the crossing with the argument register when the crossing lies within the stored range.

name: find_line_side_crossing
description: Computes a crossing of a line with one of two sides chosen by flag bits, and returns it when it lies within the stored range.

name: stub_return_only_routine
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing.

name: draw_line_into_bitplanes
description: Draws a line between two points in a four-plane bitmap with a 40-byte row stride and an error accumulator. Each step sets one pixel bit in every plane, and horizontal runs are written with per-plane colour bytes.

name: draw_line_from_stored_endpoints
description: Reads two endpoints through helper routines and draws a line in four bitplanes using the same error-accumulator stepping as its sibling, returning early when the endpoints are rejected.

name: draw_line_between_registers
description: Draws a line in the four-plane bitmap between endpoints passed in registers, using the same error-accumulator stepping as its siblings with a fixed row stride and single-bit writes to each plane.

name: draw_vertical_run_in_planes
description: Sets one pixel bit in each of four bitplanes for a counted run of rows, stepping down the bitmap by a stored row stride.

name: draw_vertical_run_from_pointer
description: Sets the same pixel bit in each of four bitplanes down a counted run of rows, starting from a pointer passed in an address register rather than computed from coordinates.

name: draw_steep_line_segment
description: Draws a line segment in four bitplanes that moves one row per step, using an error accumulator to decide when to advance to the next byte column. One pixel bit is set in every plane per step.

name: draw_steep_line_from_pointer
description: Draws the same one-row-per-step line as its sibling routine, starting from a pointer passed in an address register and using the stored row stride.

name: fill_horizontal_run_in_planes
description: Sets a horizontal run of pixels in four bitplanes, writing the leading partial byte bit by bit, then whole bytes with per-plane colour bytes, then the trailing bits.

name: fill_horizontal_run_from_pointer
description: Performs the same horizontal run fill as its sibling routine, starting from a pointer passed in an address register. The empty routine it references does nothing.

name: draw_shallow_line_segment
description: Draws a line segment in four bitplanes that advances horizontally by an error accumulator, setting pixel bits along each row and stepping down by a row stride when the accumulator crosses.

name: draw_shallow_line_from_pointer
description: Draws the same shallow line as its sibling routine, starting from a pointer passed in an address register and using the stored row stride.

name: store_point_and_call_routine
description: Stores the two 16-bit halves of its argument into a pair of base-relative slots, then calls another routine.

name: store_point_pair_and_return
description: Stores the two halves of its argument into the same pair of slots as its sibling routine and calls one routine. It returns with no meaningful value in the result registers.

name: plot_point_if_within_bounds
description: Checks a point against four stored bounds and, when it lies inside them, offsets its vertical position and sets the matching pixel bit in each of four bitplanes.

name: set_pixel_bit_at_pointer
description: Sets one pixel bit in each of four bitplanes at a byte pointer passed in an address register, using a bit index taken from a register.

name: clear_block_longwords_backwards
description: Clears a block of bitplane memory by storing zero 32-bit words in an unrolled loop, working backwards from a row pointer computed from a stored row span. It repeats this across a number of row groups.

name: emit_scaled_table_values
description: Divides a 32-bit field from a stored record by its argument and passes the quotient to library entry points. It then repeats similar divisions over several tables in counted loops, using a fixed divisor of minus 10000 in one step.

name: project_and_emit_point_table
description: Projects a table of points by dividing scaled coordinates by a depth value offset by 600, and computes paired offsets around each projected value. Results that lie within stored bounds are passed to a library entry point.

name: draw_fixed_text_labels
description: Makes a series of drawing calls at fixed screen positions with string pointers, around one library entry point call, then clears two state words to zero. The referenced text includes difficulty names, wave labels, bonus options, prompt wording and two numeric amounts.

name: update_countdown_display_and_mode
description: Writes one digit derived from a stored timer into a text buffer and draws it beside the countdown label. It then runs a sequence of state checks; when one passes it sets a mode value and a flag word, otherwise it draws a fixed set of line coordinates and an extra item when a routine returns a nonzero value.

name: run_prompt_selection_loop
description: Draws the prompt text asking the player to wait for information or pull the trigger, together with two positioned labels. It then loops over a three-state selector, calling a polling routine until the state reaches its end value, and finally redraws the text and clears the state.

name: wait_for_state_or_timeout
description: Repeatedly calls a set of routines while a state word is zero and a counter stays below 500, then clears a stored value. It returns a negative status when no state was set and otherwise a flag that is zero only when the state equals 4.

name: build_128_entry_offset_table
description: Fills a 128-entry table of point triples by deriving each entry from a stored source table with shifts and fixed offsets of 100 and 2000, using two conversion calls with a constant of minus 140 per entry. It then sets two base-relative fields.

name: draw_credits_text_block
description: Draws four credit lines at offsets from a stored horizontal position and then copies a fixed-size block of bitplane data to the display. The referenced text holds the publisher, version and title credits.

name: draw_story_text_block
description: Draws eight lines of narrative text at increasing vertical offsets from a stored position and then copies a fixed-size block to the display. The referenced text describes rebels, the empire, a death star and the force.

name: decode_unavailable_routine_body
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code exists. The facts show only that it is entered from two unnamed callers and spans 47 instructions, so its behaviour cannot be stated from the evidence.

name: update_128_entry_offset_table
description: Adds scaled values, derived from two conversion calls on a stored counter, to a 128-entry table of point offsets and copies stored values into a second buffer. The counter increases when the argument is above ten and its low two bits are both set.

name: inspect_unavailable_routine_body
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code exists. The facts show only that it is entered from one unnamed caller and spans 30 instructions, and nothing more can be stated about its behaviour.

name: draw_vertex_pairs_with_offset
description: Draws a fixed sequence of vertex pairs read from a stored table, calling two drawing entry points per vertex, with the second taking a stored offset added to each value. A timing routine is called before the sequence begins.

name: run_timed_frame_sequence
description: Runs three counted sequences of frames, each frame calling helper routines, busy-waiting until a timer word advances, and drawing with an adjusted vertical value. It returns early with a status when a helper returns nonzero and otherwise returns zero.

name: select_stage_result_code
description: Calls a routine and, when its result is nonzero, passes that result to another routine. It then returns a code from zero to three chosen by a counter compared with thresholds of 20 and 300, an argument value and a pending flag, clearing the flag when it returns three.

name: update_record_table_with_respawn
description: Advances a table of records by a per-record velocity and draws each one, respawning a record with fresh values from a helper call when it passes a bound. The sign of the argument chooses which axis is checked and which velocity is applied.

name: initialise_record_table_randomly
description: Fills a table of seventy three-field records with values from a helper routine, storing the high bytes of two draws and a count from one to eight derived from a third draw.

name: draw_briefing_text_for_index
description: Selects one of about fifteen text blocks from an index argument and draws it at a position offset from a stored column with a fixed row offset, then restores the previous buffer pointer. The referenced text covers flight instructions and mission briefing points, such as collisions, shields, laser towers and trench turrets.

name: draw_scoring_legend_table
description: Draws a scoring legend with labelled rows for targets such as tie fighters, laser towers, trench turrets and the exhaust port, pairing each label with a point value such as 1,000 or 50,000. It then copies a fixed-size block to the display.

name: run_timed_sweep_sequence
description: Runs a sequence of up to 768 frames, each waiting for a timer tick and drawing with an offset that steps down every five frames once a threshold is passed. It returns the status of its first helper call when that call reports a break.

name: run_timed_sweep_variant
description: Performs the same frame sequence as its sibling routine, with the same counter, timer wait and offset steps, and calls a few further routines between frames. It returns the status from the helper call that reports a break.

name: run_timed_downward_sweep
description: Runs a downward frame sequence from a starting counter of 110 until it reaches minus 360, drawing each frame and stepping an offset down every five frames once the counter is below minus 300. It waits for a timer tick on each frame and returns the status of its helper when that helper reports a break.

name: store_indexed_table_entry
description: Stores the high 16-bit word of its argument in a 16-entry word table, with the entry selected by the low four bits of the argument's low word.

name: wait_until_timer_reaches
description: Resets a 16-bit timer word to zero and spins until it reaches the value passed in the argument.

name: compute_integer_square_root
description: Iterates Newton's method toward the integer square root of its argument, starting from the argument divided by 200 plus two, and returns once the estimate stops changing. The final estimate is held in a local variable and is not returned to the caller.

name: stub_empty_gap_routine
description: Contains only a return instruction in a gap that the disassembler decoded as code, so it does nothing.

name: set_default_bounds_small
description: Sets three base-relative words to fixed defaults of 15, minus 15 and 15, values used as small extents by the point and line routines.

name: set_default_viewport_bounds
description: Sets six base-relative words to fixed default extents and bounds: a pair of horizontal limits at minus 160 and 159, a width-like value of 160, a height-like value of 115, and a pair of vertical limits at minus 84 and 84.

name: advance_record_positions_with_wrap
description: Moves a table of thirty records by a speed argument and wraps each position by a fixed span when it passes a limit, choosing the upper or lower limit from the sign of the speed. Each record is drawn through helper calls, with a second draw when a stored comparison value says so.

name: advance_records_wrap_below_limit
description: Steps a counted run of records by a speed, wrapping any position that falls below minus 500 by a fixed span, and calls drawing helpers for each record.

name: advance_records_wrap_above_limit
description: Steps thirty records by a speed and wraps any position above 14000 back by a fixed span, then calls drawing helpers for each record and draws it again when a stored comparison value says so.

name: advance_counted_records_wrap_above
description: Steps a counted run of records by a speed, wraps any position above 14000 by a fixed span, and calls drawing helpers for each record.

name: advance_records_reflect_on_wrap
description: Advances thirty records by a speed and, when a position wraps, negates the record's two velocity fields. For positive speeds it also updates two coordinates from scaled stored values with twelve-bit wrapping, then draws each record through a helper.

name: advance_records_twelve_bit_wrap
description: Steps a counted run of records by a speed, reflecting the velocity fields when a position falls below minus 500. It then adds two offsets to each record's coordinates with twelve-bit wrapping and draws each record.

name: advance_records_reflect_above_limit
description: Steps thirty records by a speed and, when a position exceeds 14000, wraps it back by a fixed span and negates the record's two velocity fields. Each record is then drawn through a helper.

name: advance_counted_records_reflect
description: Steps a counted run of records by a speed, wrapping and reflecting any record whose position exceeds 14000, and draws each record through a helper.

name: draw_frame_with_timer_wait
description: Resets a timer word, makes a sequence of drawing calls that use the argument twice, then waits until the timer advances before making one final call.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Makes one call to a library entry point with no arguments and returns.

name: pop_stack_entries_while_matching
description: Walks backwards through a stack of six-byte entries while each entry's first word is at or above the argument and the pointer stays within the stack bounds. It calls a routine for each entry, reduces a stored count by six, and writes the final pointer back to the base-relative area.

name: claim_matching_entry_slot
description: Walks an array of six-word entries, skipping those whose key is at or below the argument, until one passes a two-field test. It then makes a call, moves that entry's position by a scaled fraction of stored offsets, and marks it with a negative state word, returning minus one; it returns zero when the scan finishes without a match.

name: insert_entry_in_sorted_list
description: Finds the first six-byte entry whose key exceeds the argument within a counted range, increments a stored count, and calls a helper with that entry and the following one to shift the list. It returns the position found.

name: emit_entry_records_with_reciprocal
description: Writes one output triple for each active list entry, copying two stored words and a value equal to 25600 divided by the entry's key plus 600. When the argument is nonzero it also passes each entry to a helper routine.

name: update_entry_list_and_prune
description: Advances a list of six-word entries by subtracting a stored step from each key and adding velocity fields, wrapping the lateral coordinate within a twelve-bit range. It removes leading expired entries and then any entry whose vertical field falls below minus 22, calling a helper to compact the list.

name: draw_six_entry_symmetric_pattern
description: Scales a table of six entries by a stored factor and, for each entry, plots three symmetric point pairs around a centre using the two alternating drawing routines. The sign of the argument selects one of two variants that differ in where a no-argument call occurs, and a stored phase advances by 288 per entry before being reduced by 1440 at the end.

name: set_parameters_from_counter
description: Derives three stored parameters from a counter, each switching to a fixed value once the counter reaches a threshold. It then calls a helper routine and increments the counter up to 99.

name: review_unavailable_routine_body
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code exists. The facts show only that it is entered through a handler pointer and makes one unnamed call across ten instructions, and its purpose cannot be stated from the evidence.

name: plot_word_sequence_from_table
description: Calls one drawing entry point for each word of a table, stepping through the table two bytes at a time for a counted number of words, and returns the pointer just past the table.

name: forward_pair_to_drawing_calls
description: Passes a word argument to one drawing entry point and a long argument to another, then returns. The disassembler decoded this routine from a gap in the code.

name: call_routine_eleven_times
description: Makes eleven consecutive calls to one no-argument routine and returns.

name: run_timed_update_until_limit
description: Clears several state words and loops while a helper reports no event, a flag stays clear and a timer word is below 1500. Each pass calls a helper with a constant of 900, draws, waits for a tick and reduces a local step value by 250 once it exceeds 1000; afterwards it drains a second helper and makes a final call with a stored value.

name: run_timed_update_counting
description: Repeats a timed loop that draws, waits for a tick, reduces a local step value by 250 once it exceeds 1000 and increments a counter. It stops when a helper reports an event, a flag is set or a timer passes 1500, then drains a second helper and makes a final call with a stored value.

name: drain_helper_then_final_call
description: Clears a flag word, calls a helper repeatedly until it reports no pending work and the flag reads zero, then makes one final call with a stored value.

name: draw_zigzag_point_pairs
description: Draws a zigzag pattern of point pairs at fixed offsets by calling two drawing entry points for each pair. The number of repeats scales with the argument, and the horizontal position advances in steps of 14 in the first loop and 6 in the second.

name: draw_shield_status_indicator
description: Draws the shield status by choosing one of three constants from threshold tests on a stored level, drawing one of two labels, and reducing a counter above one while drawing a marker, then copies a fixed-size block to the display. The referenced text covers the shield and shield-gone labels.

name: adjust_shield_counter_by_delta
description: When a state word equals one it adds the argument to a stored counter and makes a helper call. A negative argument first calls a helper with a constant of three and, if the counter is not positive, resets several state words and returns.

name: start_counter_from_record_delta
description: Copies a stored counter into a state word, sets another state word to ten, adds a value from the caller's record to the counter, and makes a helper call.

name: handle_pause_and_flag_commands
description: Dispatches on a command code: code 64 pauses by waiting for a helper to report nothing pending, drawing the 'Game Paused' label, waiting for a resume input and restoring the display pointer, while codes 80 and 81 set and clear a flag byte and code 82 toggles a byte.

name: draw_status_markers_and_glyphs
description: Draws status markers chosen by a mode word: a pair of lines in one mode, and a blinking glyph in another. Two timed markers decrement and blink while their counters are nonzero, then a fixed glyph made of point pairs is drawn and the mode word is cleared.

name: draw_blinking_glyphs_and_timers
description: Draws the blinking glyph and the two timed markers, then a fixed point-pair glyph. It stores a helper result in a record field, calls another helper when that result is nonzero, and clears the mode word.

name: draw_offset_glyph_and_timers
description: Draws a fixed point-pair glyph at an offset from its argument, then the two timed markers and a second glyph. It stores a helper result in a record field and calls another helper when that result is nonzero.

name: draw_timed_markers_and_glyph
description: Draws one timed marker that blinks while its counter is nonzero, then a fixed point-pair glyph. It stores a helper result in a record field, calls another helper when that result is nonzero, and clears the mode word.

name: draw_paired_point_glyphs
description: Draws two fixed point-pair glyphs at offsets on either side of a stored position, stores a helper result in a record field, calls another helper when it is nonzero, and clears the mode word.

name: update_motion_offsets_and_flags
description: Computes display offsets from stored values and helper results, and clamps two velocity fields to plus or minus 270 and plus or minus 320 when a control flag is clear. It updates two offsets as a weighted average of their previous value and a velocity, and when a pending flag is set it clears it, toggles a byte and starts a countdown before calling a helper.

name: update_motion_offsets_from_locals
description: Performs the same offset and velocity update as its sibling routine, computing the scaled difference from local values first and applying the same clamps when the control flag is clear.

name: damp_offsets_with_clamp_upper
description: Clamps one velocity field to an upper limit of 270 and a second to plus or minus 320, updates two offsets as weighted averages toward their velocities, and handles the pending flag like its siblings.

name: damp_offsets_clamp_lateral
description: Clamps a lateral velocity field to an upper limit of 320, updates two offsets as weighted averages toward their velocities, and handles the pending flag like its siblings.

name: start_countdown_and_call_helper
description: Sets one countdown counter to seven and calls a helper with a zero argument.

name: draw_number_digits_with_separator
description: Draws a number one four-bit digit at a time from the low end, placing a separator pair of points after every fourth digit. It stops when no nonzero digits remain or after eight digits.

name: tick_flash_countdown_when_zero
description: Decrements a countdown word and, when it reaches zero, draws a pair of points using the alternate display buffer before making one further call.

name: reset_flash_countdown_and_draw
description: Makes setup calls, sets the flash countdown to ten, and then copies a block sized 15 by 29 to the display.

name: draw_small_block_flagged
description: Draws a fixed point, calls a helper once or twice depending on whether a stored byte is below ten, and copies a block sized four by eleven to the display.

name: draw_block_with_count_threshold
description: Makes setup calls, draws a fixed glyph once or twice depending on whether the argument is below ten, and copies a block sized 17 by 24 to the display.

name: layout_five_item_slots
description: Computes two scale values from differences of stored coordinates, then draws five items at positions offset from a computed centre, each using its own record buffer.

name: fill_rotation_table_entries
description: Advances two stored angle values, then fills a table of six pairs of lookup results by calling two lookup routines with the angle, stepping the angle by 288 per entry. A few further lookups at fixed offsets are also stored.

name: draw_decreasing_gap_column
description: Calls one drawing routine repeatedly with a fixed second argument of 250, while the first argument counts down from 1300 to zero in steps that shrink from 46 to 4 as it goes.

name: draw_selected_point_pattern
description: Selects one of ten small point patterns from a case number and draws it at the argument position by writing an origin pair to base-relative slots and calling a drawing entry point with each pattern's offsets.

name: draw_text_string_glyphs
description: Draws a null-terminated string character by character, advancing by a stored spacing value on each space. Letters and punctuation are drawn as small point patterns chosen by a switch on the character code, with a character-class table selecting the drawing path.

name: handle_initials_entry_key
description: Scans up to thirty key-table entries for the selected character using input-state reads, stores the chosen character in the entry buffer and draws it. The characters '1', '2' and '3' take different drawing paths.

name: append_character_to_entry_buffer
description: Adds the selected character to a three-character entry buffer, with code '1' ending the entry, code '2' appending a space, code '3' removing the last character, and any other code appended while there is room. It returns a status that is nonzero while the entry remains open.

name: draw_status_label_with_value
description: Computes a display value from a stored value and a flag byte, sets a scaled offset, and draws a labelled value through a helper. It then clears a pending flag by calling another helper with zero.

name: run_high_score_table_screen
description: Draws the high-score table with ten ranked rows, each showing a formatted rank, a three-character name and a score, and highlights the row matching the argument. When the argument is the sentinel value it shows the rebel command message and waits for a timed period; otherwise it runs an initials-entry loop for the highlighted row.

name: insert_score_into_top_ten
description: Sums nine values from a helper into a total, then inserts the total into a ten-entry table of eight-byte records in descending order. Lower entries are shifted down to make room, and a helper is called afterwards.

name: insert_total_into_top_ten
description: Accumulates helper values into a total while shifting a stored value right by four bits on each pass. It then inserts the 32-bit total into a ten-entry table of 32-bit scores at the first position where it is at least as large, and calls a helper.

name: insert_value_into_sorted_ten
description: Scans a ten-entry table of 32-bit values for the first entry the argument is at least as large as, shifts the entries below it down, and inserts the argument there before calling a helper. It returns without change when no position is found.

name: setup_timer_io_request
description: Creates a message port and an I/O request block, opens a device through a library entry point and sends two requests through the same block. The sequence includes a delay wrapper and a library vector call, and it releases the resources when setup fails or completes.

name: clear_flag_and_call_library
description: Clears a global word and then calls a routine with a fixed code value. That call chain reaches a library stub that calls the library function at an offset of minus 30 from its base.

name: scan_disk_track_sync
description: Configures disk controller registers for a track read, waits on a ready flag with a bounded count, and scans the buffer for the standard track sync word. It returns when enough words follow the sync word; otherwise it clears a global and calls a recovery routine.

name: reset_round_state_hints
description: Resets a set of round state words and computes a stored value from a level counter, multiplying it by 15 up to a cap of 90 and adding 80. When a display flag is set it draws the hint labels 'Shoot Fireballs' and 'Shoot Tie-Fighters' and copies two blocks to the display.

name: advance_records_with_angle_offsets
description: Moves thirty records by a fixed step, wrapping keys that fall below minus 500, shifts their two coordinates by negated stored offsets with twelve-bit wrapping, and draws each record through a helper.

name: compute_record_offsets_from_angles
description: Looks up two values from a table at an angle taken from a record field offset by 360, then stores them as quarter-scaled words in that record's fields.

name: spawn_record_when_slot_free
description: When the active count is below a stored limit and a stored counter exceeds 100, fills the next free record with positions and velocities drawn from helper values, marks a slot as occupied, sets default fields and a special flag, and records a timer value of 300.

name: update_active_record_table
description: Advances each active record by its velocity and countdown fields, sometimes re-picking velocities from helper values, and draws records that remain alive. It removes records whose countdown falls below minus 55 and resets per-record fields when a level counter reaches 100, calling a helper when it reaches 20.

name: assign_targets_to_active_records
description: Scans active records and, when a helper check and a bounds test both pass, sets a record's position and velocity from stored coordinates divided by a stored scale. The scan stops when the record count or a stored limit is reached.

name: run_alternating_library_pair_calls
description: Makes thirteen calls that alternate between two library entry points, each taking no arguments, and returns the result registers unchanged.

name: draw_record_outline_points
description: Draws the outline of a record by plotting points taken from fixed field offsets of the record, alternating two drawing entry points and finishing with two extra points.

name: draw_record_segment_pattern
description: Draws a record's segments with one or two drawing calls at offsets chosen by a state field. When a further flag is set it draws four groups of point pairs and five more pairs read from a pattern table held in the record.

name: detect_record_hits_and_update
description: Scans active records for one that falls within stored bounds on helper-sampled tests, and on a hit sets a flag and adjusts its velocity and countdown fields. It then recomputes a range pointer and draws each active record through helpers.

name: remove_random_record_from_list
description: Scans a list of six-word records for one whose first field is at or above minus 401 and whose second field is non-negative, and passes helper checks. On a match it moves the last record into that slot, reduces the count and calls a helper.

name: update_totals_and_countdown_flags
description: Once a level counter reaches 100, reduces two 32-bit totals by scaled stored values, and otherwise sets a fixed value of 200. It toggles a flag byte when a pending flag is set, starts a countdown and calls a helper.

name: draw_advancing_marker_bar
description: When a flag byte is set and an advancing counter remains below 320, draws a short bar at fixed positions whose vertical extent depends on a status bit, using the block copy routine.

name: draw_totals_readout
description: Draws a readout of two 32-bit totals. While the level counter is below 111 it draws a value derived from that counter; otherwise it computes two quotients from the totals, shifts each right by six, stores them and draws the second.

name: draw_each_record_timed_value
description: Calls one routine for each active record with the record's field and a fixed value of 300.

name: run_frame_loop_until_flag
description: Runs frames while a stored counter stays non-negative and a flag is clear, drawing each frame and waiting for a timer tick. Once the flag is set it resets two state words and calls a helper, then clears a second flag and returns the first flag's value.

name: scale_lookup_by_ten_thousand
description: Passes its argument to a helper, looks up a value using a fixed argument of 10000, and returns that value shifted right by thirteen bits.

name: forward_call_to_one_routine
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It has no other logic.

name: append_pair_to_output_buffer
description: Writes two 16-bit values, each stored as a 32-bit integer, into the output buffer whose pointer is held in a base-relative slot, then advances that pointer by eight bytes.

name: build_helper_value_buffers
description: Fills an output buffer with pairs of helper values in a loop, then fills a second region with helper values offset by 7500 and minus 10000. It finishes by calling a drawing routine with twenty-one fixed argument values.

name: initialise_record_ramp_table
description: Initialises thirty records whose first field steps from minus 259 by 483 per record, and fills their other two fields with helper values shifted right by twelve bits.

name: delay_after_ten_calls
description: Makes ten calls to one routine with the same global argument, then spins through a loop of two million iterations before returning.

name: initialise_shape_record_table
description: Zeroes the first field of six records and registers six shape entries with a loader routine. The referenced names are shape data files for laser shots, a nose shape and a star shape.

name: load_named_shape_resource
description: Loads a named resource through a library entry point, stores the returned handle and a parameter in the caller's record, allocates a buffer for it, and calls a further library entry point to finish loading.

name: load_sound_and_shape_assets
description: Loads sound and shape resources by name through a loader routine, clears a table of eleven entries and formats a numeric value into a text buffer, then packs pairs of its digits into bytes. The referenced file names cover several sound effects and shape files.

name: allocate_game_buffers_table
description: Clears a set of buffer pointers, allocates buffers of fixed sizes through a library allocator, and fills a sixteen-entry word table with fixed constants.

name: show_return_key_prompt
description: Draws the 'Return key' prompt from a list buffer at a fixed position using three positioned draw calls and one library call, then makes a final library call.

name: reset_game_state_variables
description: Sets a large group of game state words, counters and flags to starting values, and clears a 31-entry table. It then calls a helper and copies a block whose size is packed into a single argument to the display.
